title: Detroit man sentenced to up to 20 years for role in auto theft ring
text:
Detroit man sentenced to up to 20 years for role in auto theft ring
Caesar Cooper, 25, of Detroit, was sentenced on Aug. 12 to five to twenty years’ incarceration after pleading guilty in June to one count of Conducting a Criminal Enterprise for his involvement in an extensive auto theft ring, Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel announced. The sentencing took place before Judge Cheryl A. Matthews in the 6th Circuit Court in Oakland County.
Cooper was originally charged in November 2025 with one count of Conducting a Criminal Enterprise and two counts of Receiving and Concealing Stolen Property - Motor Vehicle. Authorities said he was responsible for numerous vehicle thefts across Metro Detroit from 2023 through 2025, including models such as a Lincoln Navigator, Maserati Levante, Jeep Grand Cherokee, Cadillac Escalade, and Dodge Durango.
The Attorney General’s office first announced the investigation into the auto theft operation in May 2024. The Troy Police Department began investigating the crime ring in August 2023 and later partnered with the FORCE Team early in 2024 to address what officials described as an expansive criminal organization targeting new vehicle storage lots at manufacturing facilities, car dealerships, parking lots, and private residences. Multiple local police agencies contributed to the investigation along with specialized county units focused on auto theft.
Since last year, fifteen defendants have been sentenced for their roles within this criminal network.
“Working alongside the Troy Police Department and law enforcement across Metro Detroit, the FORCE Team has been able to hold more than a dozen individuals accountable for their roles in dangerous auto thefts,” said Attorney General Nessel. “Their dedicated work over the past few years has undoubtedly made our communities safer, and we remain committed to dismantling this prolific criminal network.”
The FORCE Team was established by the Attorney General’s office in January 2023 as a specialized unit focused on targeting organizations that steal products from retailers for resale profit. The team includes two assistant attorneys general working full time alongside special agents from both state agencies and federal partners such as the FBI’s Detroit Fraud and Financial Crimes Task Force and Postal Inspection Service.
